claim_to_evidence.domain: all positive n with exactly six distinct prime factors; prime powers may have any exponent

correctness.rationale: For prime-power components Q_i ordered by size, unitary-totient weights are the 2^r products of Q_i-1. A missing-sum argument and interval induction prove exact equivalence to Q_i<=M_(i-1)+2. The bound M_i<=2^(2^i)-1 is monotone with equality only at consecutive Fermat components. If M_5<G_5, M_6<=G_5^2-1; otherwise the sixth prime power is at most 2^32 since 2^32+1=641*6700417 has two distinct prime factors. The attained product 2^32*(2^32-1) is therefore the unique maximum. The embedded checker independently verified 641 and 6700417 primality by exact trial division, arithmetic, 1252 small bitset cases and 15 initial sequence examples. Universal inference rests on the proof, not those cases.

value.rationale: The maximum over exactly r distinct prime supports is a canonical extremal invariant for an established sequence, not a chosen finite interval. The first five support sizes attain the universal greedy envelope 2^(2^r)-1; six is the first failure because the next Fermat number is composite. The theorem computes the exact optimal deficit and proves uniqueness. This is a motivated natural transition with structural explanatory content beyond membership tables or a bare finite check.
